item: Splice: the contraction x_q = y_q = t, coefficient of t, turning the stable permutation-law symbol into a stable symbol of the 2^{#pin-free cycles}-weighted next-pin law (loop weight 2; Heisenberg magnetization)
lean_status_why: The splice, its action on permutation symbols (fixed point gives a factor 2, otherwise the path is spliced), stability preservation and the cycle-weight bookkeeping are all formalized and lie on the proof DAG of the comparator OAI.Heisenberg.spontaneous_magnetization, matching lem:pin-splicing of the Sep 24 paper.
lean_gaps: Checked at text level only; the Lean was not compiled (no local toolchain).
Lean splices one vertex at a time (Option V -> V) and iterates by strong induction on |V| in stable_pinLaw; the paper deletes all non-pins at once. Equivalent.
Lean laws are finite mixtures (Fintype Ω with weights μ); Poisson exchange laws enter through limits elsewhere (PolynomialLimits.lean, Hurwitz), not in PinSplicing.
Lean 'Stable' means nonvanishing on the open upper half-plane, with nonzero-ness proved separately (lawSymbol_ne_zero_general). This matches the paper's 'stable up to zero' convention.

The cycle weight 2^{n_P} is tracked by missingCount (Nat.card of MissingClasses), and cycle_weight_splice shows it factorizes under one splice. Output extraction G_T is in stable_outputSymbol / stable_pinDensity, not in PinSplicing.

Only the half-plane (B+C) splice is formalized. The disk / A+D contraction of the spherical companion, and the Bloch and lattice-correction companions, are not in the Lean (lean/docs/271.md covers only the Sep 24 theorem).
No declaration in PinSplicing.lean has a docstring.
The dominated share of stable_spliced_law in the comparator DAG is small (0.013 per extract_lean.py), but it cannot be bypassed: every pin-test path goes through stable_pinLaw -> stable_spliced_law.

lean_source.name: OAI.Heisenberg.Pin.spliceVariables
lean_source.text:
def spliceVariables : Option V ⊕ Option V → Option (V ⊕ V)
  | Sum.inl none => none
  | Sum.inr none => none
  | Sum.inl (some i) => some (Sum.inl i)
  | Sum.inr (some i) => some (Sum.inr i)

lean_source.name: OAI.Heisenberg.Pin.eraseNone
lean_source.text:
def eraseNone {σ : Type*} : MvPolynomial (Option σ) ℂ →ₐ[ℂ] MvPolynomial σ ℂ :=
  MvPolynomial.aeval (fun j => j.elim 0 MvPolynomial.X)

lean_source.name: OAI.Heisenberg.Pin.splice
lean_source.text:
def splice (p : MvPolynomial (Option V ⊕ Option V) ℂ) : MvPolynomial (V ⊕ V) ℂ :=
  eraseNone (MvPolynomial.pderiv none (MvPolynomial.rename spliceVariables p))

lean_source.name: OAI.Heisenberg.Pin.spliceWeight
lean_source.text: def spliceWeight (π : Equiv.Perm (Option V)) : ℝ := if π none = none then 2 else 1

lean_source.name: OAI.Heisenberg.Pin.splice_permutationSymbol_fixed
lean_source.text:
theorem splice_permutationSymbol_fixed (π : Equiv.Perm (Option V)) (h : π none = none) :
    splice (permutationSymbol π) = 2 * permutationSymbol (Equiv.removeNone π)

lean_source.name: OAI.Heisenberg.Pin.splice_permutationSymbol_nonfixed
lean_source.text:
theorem splice_permutationSymbol_nonfixed (π : Equiv.Perm (Option V))
    (h : π none ≠ none) :
    splice (permutationSymbol π) = permutationSymbol (Equiv.removeNone π)

lean_source.name: OAI.Heisenberg.Pin.stable_splice
lean_source.text:
theorem stable_splice {p : MvPolynomial (Option V ⊕ Option V) ℂ}
    (hp : Stable p) (hn : splice p ≠ 0) : Stable (splice p)

lean_source.name: OAI.Heisenberg.Pin.stable_spliced_law
lean_source.text:
theorem stable_spliced_law (μ : Ω → ℝ) (π : Ω → Equiv.Perm (Option V))
    (hμ : ∀ ω, 0 ≤ μ ω) (hpos : 0 < ∑ ω, μ ω) (hs : Stable (lawSymbol μ π)) :
    Stable (lawSymbol (fun ω => μ ω * spliceWeight (π ω))
      (fun ω => Equiv.removeNone (π ω)))

lean_source.name: OAI.Heisenberg.Cycle.cycle_weight_splice
lean_source.text:
theorem cycle_weight_splice (π : Perm (Option V)) (P : Set V) :
    (2 : ℝ) ^ missingCount π (some '' P) =
      (if π none = none then 2 else 1) * (2 : ℝ) ^ missingCount (removeNone π) P

lean_source.name: OAI.Heisenberg.Pin.pinLaw
OAI.Heisenberg.Pin.stable_pinLaw
lean_source.text:
theorem stable_pinLaw {V : Type u} [Fintype V] (μ : Ω → ℝ) (π : Ω → Perm V)
    (hμ : ∀ ω, 0 ≤ μ ω) (hpos : 0 < ∑ ω, μ ω) (hs : Stable (lawSymbol μ π))
    (P : Set V) : Stable (pinLaw μ π P)

lean_source.name: OAI.Heisenberg.Pin.finite_simultaneous_pin_test
lean_source.text:
theorem finite_simultaneous_pin_test (μ : Ω → ℝ) (π : Ω → Equiv.Perm V)
    (hμ : ∀ ω, 0 ≤ μ ω) (hpos : 0 < ∑ ω, μ ω) (hs : Stable (lawSymbol μ π))
    (E : Set V) (T : Finset V) (hT : T.Nonempty) (hET : Disjoint E (T : Set V)) :
    (∑ ω, if ∀ i ∈ T, ¬ HasHit (π ω) E i then pinDensity μ π E ω else 0) ≤
      (2 * returnFraction μ π E T) ^ T.card

lean_source.name: OAI.Heisenberg.Pin.permutationSymbol
lean_source.text:
def permutationSymbol (π : Equiv.Perm V) : MvPolynomial (V ⊕ V) ℂ :=
  ∏ i, (MvPolynomial.X (Sum.inl i) + MvPolynomial.X (Sum.inr (π i)))

lean_source.name: OAI.Heisenberg.Pin.lawSymbol
lean_source.text:
def lawSymbol (μ : Ω → ℝ) (π : Ω → Equiv.Perm V) : MvPolynomial (V ⊕ V) ℂ :=
  ∑ ω, MvPolynomial.C (μ ω : ℂ) * permutationSymbol (π ω)

lean_source.name: OAI.Heisenberg.Pin.Stable
lean_source.text:
def Stable {σ : Type*} (p : MvPolynomial σ ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∀ z ∈ Upper, MvPolynomial.eval z p ≠ 0

speedup_targets.title: Suzuki–Fisher Lee–Yang theorem for the spin-1/2 quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet
speedup_targets.statement: For a finite graph with ferromagnetic couplings J_xy >= 0 (isotropic, or XXZ with |Delta| <= 1), Z(h) = Tr exp(-beta H_0 + beta h sum_x S^z_x) has all its zeros in e^{-beta h} on the unit circle; equivalently Z != 0 when Re h != 0, also for site-dependent fields with real parts of one sign.
speedup_targets.reference: M. Suzuki, M. E. Fisher, J. Math. Phys. 12 (1971) 235–246; T. Asano, PRL 24 (1970) 1409 and J. Phys. Soc. Japan 29 (1970) 350; restated as Thms 45–47 of Harrow–Mehraban–Soleimanifar, arXiv:1910.09071.
speedup_targets.current_proof_size: About 10–12 journal pages in SF71 (Trotter mapping to a classical multilayer model, an Asano contraction per layer, then a limit). No formalization found in Mathlib or elsewhere.
speedup_targets.how_item_helps: In Toth's loop representation with a site field, a closed loop of length L gets weight z^{L/2} + z^{-L/2} instead of 2. The spherical companion does exactly this with the disk symbol E prod(1 + x_i y_pi(i)) and the A+D contraction (Lemma trace-zero-free). That contraction step replaces SF71's Trotter-to-Ising mapping. The Lean has only the half-plane splice (the B+C coefficient), so a disk variant or a Moebius bridge must be added first.
speedup_targets.expected_speedup: med (1–2 pages instead of 10–12 for the zero-freeness core; the Lean saving is uncertain because the disk variant is missing)
speedup_targets.confidence: medium-low; this is where the device sits closest to its precedent, so a hit shows the splice can reproduce Asano/SF, not that it is new

top5.title: Suzuki–Fisher Lee–Yang via the contraction
top5.argument: This is the only known theorem whose proof the contraction itself (not the BB symbol) could shorten. The step 'trace = contract each output with its input, so each closed loop gets weight 2' replaces SF71's Trotter-to-Ising mapping. It is statable in < 300 lines from the OAI spin operators. Caveats: the Lean splice is the half-plane B+C version, so the harness must allow a disk variant; and a success shows reach toward the precedent, not novelty.

top5.argument: The one open problem that matches the obstruction exactly: theta = 2, no RP, positive simultaneous events. The statement needs only an XXZ Hamiltonian on top of the OAI model (< 300 lines). The stability half provably extends to Brauer mixtures; the presence inequality for pairings and the leakage half are open. This is the best genuine cross-model test.

precedent_check.summary: Checked against Asano 1970 and Suzuki–Fisher 1971. Asano's contraction maps A + B z1 + C z2 + D z1 z2 to A + D z and preserves zero-freeness outside products of closed sets (the disk / Lee–Yang setting). Suzuki–Fisher apply it, after a Trotter mapping, to the quantum Heisenberg model: contracting each layer's variables is a qubit trace, so every closed world-line loop gets weight 2. The splice is the half-plane sister operation: set x_q = y_q = t and take the t-coefficient, i.e. A + Bx + Cy + Dxy -> B + C. It is a composite of standard stability-preserving closure operations (diagonalization, partial derivative, real specialization: Borcea–Brändén; Wagner's survey arXiv:0911.3569, Lemma 2.4). The Lean proof stable_splice uses exactly stable_pderiv and stable_boundarySection. So 'contraction = trace = weight 2 per loop' has an earlier equivalent for this very model, in the zero-freeness setting, and the operation itself is N0. Not found anywhere: applying it to Borcea–Brändén permutation symbols to get stability, and hence BBL negative dependence, of the 2^{cycles}-weighted next-pin law. Verdict: the item is a new bridge, not a new object; the earlier equivalent of the mechanism downgrades it to N2 (agreeing with the f1 analysis).
precedent_check.post_oct6: No use of the spliced symbol outside the OAI release found (web searches for strongly Rayleigh with cycle-weighted / Toth / interchange). Ryan, arXiv:2608.21306, predates the release and uses six-vertex methods.
